figures.alt: Photo of a pack of gray wolves walking together through snow in a forest.
figures.caption: Gray wolves live in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. They hunt in packs, and groups can help members survive.

figures.alt: Photo of a gray Petoskey stone covered in many-sided cells with fine lines radiating from the middle of each, lying wet among rounded cobbles.
figures.caption: A Petoskey stone is fossil coral. It is evidence that this place was once a warm shallow sea.

figures.alt: Photo of a wetland with cattails, still water, a frog on a log and ducks.
figures.caption: A wetland is soggy land with shallow water, plants and animals. A habitat is where a living thing lives. Filling in a wetland changes who can live there. Michigan has many wetlands along the Great Lakes and inland.

figures.alt: Interactive: pick a frog, wolf or cactus and a wetland, forest, desert or tundra and see whether it lives well, less well or cannot survive.
figures.caption: Match a living thing to a habitat and see how well it fits.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Model herd: how many survived. Thick fur 8 survived, Thin fur 2 survived.
figures.caption: In a model herd, 8 animals with thick fur survived and 2 animals with thin fur survived. It is a made-up model, not wildlife data.
